standards.scope: AC/DC electrical systems used for electrical propulsion and hybrid propulsion on small craft up to 24 m LH; DC below 1500 V, single-phase AC up to 1000 V, and three-phase AC up to 1000 V.
standards.applicability_note: Directly relevant to LOS-18 electrical propulsion if vessel type, voltage and system scope match. Obtain the licensed standard and have applicability reviewed before compliance claims.

standards.scope: Measurement, evaluation and reporting of vibration for habitability on passenger and merchant ships; frequency-weighted RMS guideline values in the 1–80 Hz range for normally occupied areas; intended voyages of 24 hours or more.
standards.applicability_note: Useful measurement and reporting methodology for long-duration liveaboard trials and spatial vibration mapping. Its stated scope is passenger and merchant ships on voyages of 24 hours or more; do not automatically treat it as directly applicable statutory criteria for a private recreational craft. Low-frequency motion sickness is addressed separately by ISO 2631-1. This standard alone does not qualify seakeeping comfort or task operability.

standards.scope: Selection and installation of lithium-ion batteries and battery systems above 500 Wh used on small craft for general electrical loads and/or electric propulsion, including manufacturer safety information.
standards.applicability_note: Directly relevant to LOS-18 battery installations above 500 Wh if the craft/system falls within its stated small-craft scope. Important limit: ISO 23625 warns that boat DC systems operating at 60 V or higher have additional safety requirements not addressed by this document. Obtain the licensed standard and have a marine electrical engineer review the complete system, manufacturer requirements, voltage-specific protection, containment and applicable class/flag rules. This is not a complete high-voltage battery safety basis.

standards.scope: Standard marine test methods for air tightness and separation performance (permeation and salt rejection) of RO and NF membrane elements.
standards.applicability_note: Use as a membrane-element test reference where the exact licensed method applies. It does not qualify a complete installed yacht watermaker system, electrical energy, flush duty, potable-water safety, product storage/distribution or brine discharge.

standards.scope: Methods for measuring periodic, random and transient whole-body vibration; informative guidance on health, comfort, perception and motion sickness. Current ISO page distinguishes 0.5–80 Hz for health/comfort/perception and 0.1–0.5 Hz for motion sickness in the replacement DIS preview.

next_revision.status_as_of_2026_11_07: Final Draft International Standard registered in approval phase (stage 50.00) on 2026-09-24; under development, not yet published as replacement

standards.applicability_note: A whole-body vibration method is not by itself a validated liveaboard habitability/seakeeping model. Use task-, posture-, location-, frequency- and exposure-specific criteria; no single ISO number proves comfort.
